::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[beamer & TikZ: gradually unveil trees](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/20597/beamer-tikz-gradually-unveil-trees), asked by [Fred](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/6095/fred) on TeX Stack Exchange (2011-06-13; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> Imagine a simple tree:
>
> ```latex
> \begin{tikzpicture}
>     \node {Selbstregulation}
>     [edge from parent fork down]
>     child {node {Kognition}}
>     child {node {Metakognition}
>       child {node {Planung}}
>       child {node {Monotoring}}
>       child {node {Regulation}}
>     }
> \end{tikzpicture}
> ```
>
> Is it possible to unveil the child nodes step by step using overlays in beamer? I tried with the `\onslide` command at several positions around `child`, but it doesn't work...
>
> Any hints? - Thanks.
:::

[I have been told this is not possible][1].  [The package author wrote in 2005 that it wasn't][2].  If the ability has been added I do not know of it.

  [1]: http://osdir.com/ml/tex.latex.beamer.general/2007-02/msg00029.html
  [2]: http://comments.gmane.org/gmane.comp.tex.latex.beamer.general/432

My correspondent's advice is the best workaround that I can think of:

> To get the same effect, you may want
> to try drawing the final figure and
> then work backwards, making this
> invisible by making them have the same
> color as the background or
> transparent.
